books.section: Topic 1.6 Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
Topic 1.5 Labor, Slavery, and Caste in the Spanish Colonial System
Native Americans in Pre-Columbian North America

options.text: English settlers married Native peoples far more often than the Spanish did.
options.misconception: The contrast runs the other way: intermarriage was common in Spanish colonies and rare in English ones.

options.text: Spanish law forbade intermarriage, while English law required it.
options.misconception: No such laws existed; the difference came from who settled, not from legal bans or orders.

options.text: Spanish colonies held few Spanish women, while English colonies brought whole families.
Native peoples refused all contact with Spanish settlers but welcomed the English.
options.misconception: Native peoples traded and intermarried with the Spanish for decades; the passage describes contact, not refusal.

rationales.general:
1. Look at who got off the boats. Background: Spanish settlement was mostly men; English settlement brought whole families.
2. Ask what that difference does. Few Spanish women meant Spanish men married Native women; English families meant English settlers married each other.
3. Name the contrast. Intermarriage was common in Spanish colonies and rare in English ones.
4. Rule out the rest. No law explains it, the facts run the other way, and Native peoples did not refuse the Spanish.
Remember: to explain a contrast, find what actually differed between the two sides.
rationales.C: Spanish colonies were built by men who greatly outnumbered Spanish women, so they married Native women. English colonies later brought whole families, so English settlers married within their own communities.
rationales.A: This reverses the facts. The books say intermarriage was common in Spanish colonies and rare in English ones.
rationales.B: No law on either side ordered or forbade intermarriage. The difference came from the makeup of the settler population.
rationales.D: Native peoples had extensive contact with the Spanish, including trade and marriage. Refusal is the opposite of the record.

stem: The books note that intermarriage was common between Spanish settlers and Native peoples but rare among English settlers. Which difference best explains this contrast?

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, summarizing Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 3, Topic 1.5 and Topic 1.6; Princeton Review Chapter 6.
stimulus.text: In Spain's American colonies, Spaniards were always greatly outnumbered by Native peoples, and Spanish men greatly outnumbered Spanish women. In these circumstances, intermarriage was common. The children of Spanish men and Indigenous women were called mestizos, and they made up four to five percent of the population. The children of Spanish men and African women were called mulattos. Over time, mixing produced a large population of people of mixed ancestry.
